title: Ennis House
visualBrief: Stepped buff textile-block house above massive retaining terraces, with projecting dining-window tower, high living-room block, rear loggia, eastern master room, western motor court, bridge and garage wing. Visible 16-inch block courses and restrained Greek-key relief.

nativeAxes.x: east-southeast along the house and terraces

appearance.colorEncoding: sRGB palette decoded to linear COLOR_0

geographicProposal.groundContactBasis: Western motor-court paving at local [-18,2], model Y=0; original USGS datum independently corroborated by B23 ground returns. Raised bridge and sloping covered entrance are separate architectural levels.

terrainReference.basis: Flat western motor-court paving, visible in satellite context; avoids the sloping street outside the northwest gate.

groundCutout.basis: Only the authored sloping entrance paving beneath the bridge and its short street/court transitions. USGS B23 points show the bridge deck incorrectly represented as ground by the interpolated raster. Preserve every original height sample and the whole-house datum; the solid model floor replaces rendered ground triangles in this bounded passage. Approximate floor and registration, not a surveyed threshold.

geographicProposal.notes: Combined map polygon includes broad terrace/court platform, not one solid 16.1 m tall box. The mapped height is retained as coarse context; stepped rooms and retaining walls require separate authored heights. HABS drawing labels its long street-facing view west elevation; satellite/local frame control actual orientation. Historic house, bridge and garage/servants wing are one compound. Ground datum uses the motor court; the initial northwest street control lay on the steep approach and was replaced before authoring.

limitations: Original government HABS CA-1942 west elevation and gate detail by Jean Davis,1969, establish the textile-block hierarchy and measured15ft10.75in portal. Gate figures, rods and relief are simplified. Current condition and unseen faces are approximate; earlier attribution/private/satellite imagery is excluded from the current review.

The retained mapped full compound and HABS exterior are corroborated by public USGS B23 point measurements acquired2023-01-08 through2024-01-07. Court datum is unchanged; bridge depth/height and the raised sloping entrance are corrected as approximate architecture. This derived local registration conservatively allows2m horizontal uncertainty, without an independent epoch/datum correction; inferred under-bridge paving is not an observed navigable survey.
House, linked garage/servant wing, bridge, court, terraces and pool basin included. Interiors, vegetation, neighboring houses, vehicles, temporary scaffolds, furniture and photo pixels excluded.

Original USGS raster, review grid and source heights remain exact. A bounded rendered-ground opening exists only under the authored solid entrance paving; the original raster interpolates bridge returns across this covered passage. Isolated portable views use a flat floor below the foundations; medium-fi views retain the original ground and exercise the opening. Host datasets may differ; placement remains a preview with footprint replacement disabled.
16-inch block course spacing is retained; ornate block relief and leaded-glass geometry are simplified at medium-fi and progressively omitted at distant detail levels.
